# Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations

# Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-09 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] For Coinbase Exchange level2, size is the replacement quantity at the price level, not a delta, and zero removes a level. Binance also instructs consumers to set the new quantity and remove levels with zero quantity; adding these quantities as increments would violate both contracts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md
- [statement] A closed-trade drawdown protection is not the same quantity as a daily account loss guard including unrealized losses: Freqtrade documents the former, while Vantixs recommends the latter. Monitoring should name which loss measure each threshold actually governs. (medium confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/plugins/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://vantixs.com/blog/crypto-trading-bot-risk-limits-checklist

## Structure and components

- [statement] In Freqtrade, the documented live iteration performs distinct activities, including loading persisted trades, analyzing strategy data, and updating open-order state from the exchange. Treating evidence of one completed activity as evidence of all of them is unsupported; per-stage progress evidence is a monitor design inference from this execution structure. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/

## How it works

- [statement] Google SRE recommends paging for urgent, actionable conditions that are actively or imminently user-visible; frequent low-value pages can cause responders to ignore real incidents. Apply this criterion when deciding which bot events require immediate human attention. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/
- [statement] Google’s incident-management model assigns system modifications to the operations team, keeps a live incident document, and requires explicit acknowledgment when incident command changes hands. A bot recovery runbook can use these controls to coordinate responders and preserve continuity. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/managing-incidents/
- [statement] Google incident guidance prioritizes stopping the damage, restoring service, and preserving evidence for root-cause analysis. It assigns system modifications during an incident to the operations team, which supports a runbook with one coordinated recovery owner. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/managing-incidents/
- [statement] Freqtrade documents a systemd watchdog that can restart the bot after failures. Its documentation explicitly says the bot-to-systemd notification communication does not work when the bot runs in Docker; deployment-specific recovery mechanisms therefore need separate evaluation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/advanced-setup/
- [statement] Monitor market-data freshness per symbol and retain both exchange-event and local receive timestamps. EODHD explicitly separates these timestamps and warns that a connected feed can starve individual symbols; Freqtrade incident logs show outdated candles alongside a RUNNING process heartbeat. (medium confidence) — https://eodhd.com/financial-academy/fundamental-analysis-examples/real-time-market-data-reliability-stale-price-detection-rest-fallback-and-websocket-recovery · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/10933
- [statement] For Kraken book checksum validation, process all price-level updates in a message before calculating the checksum, delete levels with zero qty, truncate to subscribed depth after updates, and preserve price and qty precision with decimal or string decoding. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://docs.kraken.com/exchange/guides/websockets/book-checksum-v2
- [statement] For a proposed crypto-bot monitor drill suite, run a synthetic baseline and then repeat the workload with faults such as dependency disconnection, latency, process restart or thread stalls. This adapts fault-injection practices demonstrated by Microsoft and WarpStream; it is a design recommendation, not evidence of an existing bot implementation. (medium confidence) — https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/advancing-resilience-through-chaos-engineering-and-fault-injection/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.warpstream.com/blog/deterministic-simulation-testing-for-our-entire-saas
- [statement] More aggressive fault injection is not automatically better coverage. FoundationDB tunes fault distributions because excessive fault rates can confine execution to a small state space; monitor drills should therefore include intervals in which useful work and recovery can proceed. The monitor recommendation is an inference. (low confidence) — https://www.foundationdb.org/files/fdb-paper.pdf
- [statement] Kubernetes conditions include observedGeneration to identify the desired-state generation behind an observation; the conventions explicitly describe a condition as out of date when that generation lags the current generation. Bot-monitor adaptation: bind status evidence to the configuration revision it actually observed. (low confidence) — https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md
- [statement] OpenTelemetry supports optional `TraceId` and `SpanId` fields for request and span correlation; if a span identifier is present, a trace identifier should also be present. A bot evidence model can use those fields when the relevant operation has trace context. (low confidence) — https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/
- [statement] Bybit documents two Filled order messages when cancellation races with execution: one reports execution and the other reports the rejected cancellation. A monitor must not count those status messages as two independent fills. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/websocket/private/order
- [statement] NautilusTrader compares net positions per account and instrument using account quantity tolerance. When a venue reports both long and short positions, startup validation requires both side totals to match; equal net quantity alone is insufficient. Strategy ownership can also be ambiguous when several strategies share an account-level net position. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/
- [statement] A 2022 Freqtrade maintainer reply states that the bot only handled its own orders and did not expect to detect a manually closed position. The maintainer could not diagnose the reported rejection without earlier logs. This is historical scope evidence, not proof of current Freqtrade behavior or a confirmed root cause. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/6739
- [statement] NautilusTrader startup validation matches hedging positions by exact venue position identity and quantity, and netting positions by account and instrument within account tolerance. When the venue reports both long and short positions, matching only net quantity is insufficient. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/
- [statement] NautilusTrader caps targeted single-order reconciliation queries per cycle, defers remaining orders, and spaces consecutive queries to avoid venue rate limits. This provides a concrete bounded-query pattern for reconciliation after bulk-query failures. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/
- [statement] Freqtrade documents `MaxDrawdown` over closed trades in its lookback window. Its default ratios calculation uses cumulative profit ratios; its equity calculation uses starting balance and cumulative absolute profit. The guide warns these can differ when position sizes change. This closed-trade protection should not be presented as a continuously marked unrealized-loss circuit breaker. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/plugins/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] A market-data silence threshold must account for channel semantics (design inference). Coinbase ticker_batch sends every 5000 milliseconds only if there is a change, while Binance specifies 1000ms updates for 1s klines and 2000ms for other kline intervals. Silence alone therefore needs channel-specific interpretation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In a first-person bot postmortem, the alert executable was available to interactive shells but absent from the cron environment, so Telegram alerts silently failed for weeks. The author recommends a startup ping to expose notification failure. This is an attributed incident report, not an independently verified loss estimate. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/jmolinasoler/when-closed-doesnt-mean-closed-a-hyperliquid-stop-loss-post-mortem-bjl
- [statement] In the January 2025 Telegram connection-error thread, a Freqtrade maintainer said Telegram networking failure does not stop the trading bot from executing trades; the reporter confirmed the bot still worked without messages. Treat notification-channel availability and trading availability as separate incident symptoms. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/11266
- [statement] In Freqtrade issue 7299, the reporter said their timestamp-based probe restarted the container after they manually stopped the bot through Telegram. This historical example shows why a recovery policy should distinguish an intentional stop from a failure before restarting. It does not establish current behavior for every deployment. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/7299
- [statement] In the February 27, 2025 Freqtrade discussion, maintainer xmatthias explains that an old WebSocket value can reflect either a disconnect or no trades on an illiquid pair. Last-update age alone cannot identify the cause of silence. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/11269
- [statement] Deterministic failure replay requires control over nondeterministic inputs, including time, random choices, scheduling and I/O. For a bot monitor, the inferred design is to control these inputs at its dependency boundaries; replaying price records alone does not establish deterministic execution. (medium confidence) — https://antithesis.com/docs/resources/deterministic_simulation_testing/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.foundationdb.org/files/fdb-paper.pdf, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/demonic-nondeterminism/, https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/order_fill.html
- [statement] A drill needs a correctness oracle, not merely an absence of crashes. FoundationDB uses workload and local assertions; WarpStream checks message identity and monotonic sequences. Applied to a bot monitor, define expected outcomes and invariant violations before injecting each failure. (medium confidence) — https://www.foundationdb.org/files/fdb-paper.pdf · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.warpstream.com/blog/deterministic-simulation-testing-for-our-entire-saas, https://antithesis.com/docs/resources/deterministic_simulation_testing/
- [statement] A deterministic simulator still needs controlled substitutes for external dependencies. It cannot by itself establish that the real external integration behaves like its mocks; this limits what a simulated exchange can establish about a live crypto venue. (medium confidence) — https://antithesis.com/docs/resources/deterministic_simulation_testing/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://notes.eatonphil.com/2024-08-20-deterministic-simulation-testing.html
- [statement] Deterministic replay does not guarantee that the same scenario reaches the same failure after changing the binary. In its March 2024 investigation, Cockroach Labs reported instrumentation and code changes could change the terminal state; the investigation ultimately produced a reproducing unit test. The inferred practice is to preserve the failing build and scenario and add a focused regression test for the fix. (medium confidence) — https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/demonic-nondeterminism/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://notes.eatonphil.com/2024-08-20-deterministic-simulation-testing.html
- [statement] Market-data replay is not proof of realistic execution: HftBacktest states that replay cannot change market data or model market impact, and that some partial-fill scenarios remain unrealistic. Use such replay to exercise monitor behavior under recorded inputs; do not treat its fills as proof of what live orders would do. The monitor-use recommendation is an inference. (low confidence) — https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/order_fill.html
- [statement] Simulation correctness results do not establish production performance or fidelity to every dependency. The FoundationDB paper states its simulator cannot reliably detect performance problems and cannot test dependencies outside its simulation-compatible implementation. Antithesis also requires external dependencies to be controlled. For a monitor, supplement deterministic drills with checks against real dependency behavior. (medium confidence) — https://www.foundationdb.org/files/fdb-paper.pdf · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://antithesis.com/docs/resources/deterministic_simulation_testing/
- [statement] A rare failure can require correlated faults and internal transitions that ordinary stress testing misses. Cockroach Labs describes a bug diagnosed using deterministic replay and traces; WarpStream describes a failure plus scheduling race found by its fault-injecting simulator. This supports testing adversarial event orderings for monitor code, without implying a guaranteed bug-detection rate. (medium confidence) — https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/demonic-nondeterminism/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.warpstream.com/blog/deterministic-simulation-testing-for-our-entire-saas
- [statement] Historical guidance in Freqtrade issue 7299 uses the timestamp of the last bot cycle as progress evidence and compares its age with an acceptable strategy-specific cycle time; the maintainer notes that a slow strategy can take well over one minute. This is guidance from the thread, not a verified contract for every installed release. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/7299
- [statement] Design inference: observe the monitoring transport as a dependency in its own right. Hummingbot documents remote monitoring over asynchronous MQTT channels, and issue 8012 reports repeated bridge reconnect messages that made monitoring and inspection difficult; the issue report does not establish a released fix or a universal strategy failure. (medium confidence) — https://hummingbot.org/installation/broker/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8012
- [statement] Do not infer a universal healthy value from condition booleans without each condition’s semantics. Kubernetes notes that some conditions are normally true and others normally false, so a generic condition summary cannot be computed without that knowledge. This scopes any proposed single overall bot health indicator. (low confidence) — https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md
- [statement] In NautilusTrader Polymarket issue 4787, a reporter reproduced a terminal Filled report with filled quantity below original quantity, leaving the local order pending cancellation. A maintainer confirmed the mapping and required a terminal state while preserving the separate dust-underfill rule. This illustrates why quantity agreement alone cannot validate an adapter status mapping. (low confidence) — https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/4787

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For bot notification policy, distinguish suppressed events from quiet delivery and from audible notification. The inspected Freqtrade documentation distinguishes on, silent, and off; Google SRE explains why noisy paging can hide actionable incidents. This supports deliberate severity routing rather than enabling every notification equally. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/blob/develop/docs/telegram-usage.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/
- [statement] A Hyperliquid bot operator reports that the notification executable was available through the interactive shell PATH but absent for cron, and that alerts silently failed. Treat this as an attributed incident report: verify alert delivery under the actual scheduler environment rather than assuming interactive success proves unattended delivery. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/jmolinasoler/when-closed-doesnt-mean-closed-a-hyperliquid-stop-loss-post-mortem-bjl
- [statement] Google recommends randomized exponential backoff, per-request retry limits, and a server-wide retry budget, and advises against retrying permanent errors or malformed requests. Applied to bot recovery control requests and notification delivery, this supports bounded retries rather than uncontrolled retry loops; it does not establish that replaying a trading action is safe. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/
- [statement] Freshness thresholds should follow the exchange, update frequency, asset and consequence of using a stale value. EODHD explicitly labels its example thresholds as non-universal rather than a general safe timeout. (low confidence) — https://eodhd.com/financial-academy/fundamental-analysis-examples/real-time-market-data-reliability-stale-price-detection-rest-fallback-and-websocket-recovery
- [statement] A REST fallback price must retain its own source and timestamp, and should remain distinguishable from a fresh WebSocket tick. EODHD describes REST fallback as a recovery layer rather than proof that the live stream is healthy. (low confidence) — https://eodhd.com/financial-academy/fundamental-analysis-examples/real-time-market-data-reliability-stale-price-detection-rest-fallback-and-websocket-recovery
- [statement] Freqtrade documents that backtesting simulates only part of its live execution logic and that callback frequency can differ between backtesting and live iterations. A monitor drill should exercise operational behavior directly instead of treating matching backtest output as sufficient verification. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/
- [statement] Use a fault matrix that includes process restarts, network partitions, latency and delayed execution, and exercise combinations rather than only isolated failures. This is an inferred monitor-drill pattern: FoundationDB injects these classes of faults, and WarpStream describes a data-loss bug requiring both a failed flush and a rare thread interleaving. (medium confidence) — https://www.foundationdb.org/files/fdb-paper.pdf · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.warpstream.com/blog/deterministic-simulation-testing-for-our-entire-saas
- [statement] Define the simulation boundary explicitly: external dependencies must be mocked or otherwise controlled for determinism. WarpStream included clients, control-plane nodes and local storage dependencies in its test topology. Applied to a bot monitor, include controlled dependency responses and failures in the harness rather than assuming a deterministic monitor process controls external services. (medium confidence) — https://antithesis.com/docs/resources/deterministic_simulation_testing/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.warpstream.com/blog/deterministic-simulation-testing-for-our-entire-saas
- [statement] A healthy heartbeat does not prove that the service path works. The Gray Failure paper gives an example where the request handler is stuck while heartbeats remain healthy; Google SRE distinguishes internal instrumentation from tests of externally visible behavior. For bot monitoring, retain both perspectives rather than collapsing them into a heartbeat-only health assertion. (medium confidence) — https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/paper-1.pdf · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/, https://www.the-paper-trail.org/post/2020-04-19-gray-failures/
- [statement] Freqtrade issue 11957 is an attributed disagreement rather than a confirmed heartbeat-only failure: the reporter alleged stopped processing, while maintainer xmatthias challenged the inference from missing debug messages and closed the issue because the logs did not establish the problem. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/11957
- [statement] Design inference: keep desired operation separate from observed bot status, and expose multiple named health conditions instead of assuming that a single running label describes every behavior. Kubernetes separates desired intent from status and supports multiple conditions; the gray-failure example shows why process-level health can diverge from useful work. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.the-paper-trail.org/post/2020-04-19-gray-failures/
- [statement] Design inference: define progress against the work the bot is expected to perform, rather than demanding an arbitrary log message on every heartbeat. Freqtrade documents a repeated loop with candle-scoped work; the disputed issue demonstrates that absence of analysis messages at regular log levels does not establish absence of processing. (medium confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/11957
- [statement] External checks and internal evidence serve complementary purposes: Google SRE says black-box checks expose active symptoms but are poor at predicting imminent problems, whereas white-box instrumentation can expose imminent problems and failures masked by retries. A monitor evidence model should retain the observation method instead of treating these observations as interchangeable. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/
- [statement] Reconcile orders, fills, and positions separately: NautilusTrader processes venue order and fill reports before checking positions, while Freqtrade updates exchange order state before verifying existing positions. This supports a monitor that compares execution state with venue exposure rather than treating an open-order list as a position ledger. (medium confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/
- [statement] Order status and fill quantity are distinct reconciliation inputs. CCXT describes one order producing multiple fills; Bybit exposes remaining quantity, cumulative executed quantity, and average fill price separately. A monitor should compare executed quantities rather than infer execution volume from status-event counts. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/websocket/private/order

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Design inference: test alert delivery from the actual scheduled execution environment and monitor the notification path separately from trading. A first-person bot postmortem reports simultaneous trading and alerting failures, while Google SRE recommends combining internal telemetry with external behavior checks. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/jmolinasoler/when-closed-doesnt-mean-closed-a-hyperliquid-stop-loss-post-mortem-bjl · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/
- [statement] In a September 2024 Freqtrade issue, a user still received entry and exit notifications while commands stopped responding. A maintainer explained that sharing one Telegram bot across two Freqtrade instances can disrupt incoming updates while outgoing notifications still work. Recovery diagnosis therefore needs separate checks for both directions. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/10681
- [statement] Google’s incident-management guidance prioritizes stopping the damage, restoring service, and preserving evidence. It recommends documenting incident procedures in advance. These are appropriate runbook priorities for a bot alert that requires human recovery. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/managing-incidents/
- [statement] The September 2025 report that Freqtrade Telegram integration was completely broken is disputed: the reporter described silent commands, but the maintainer identified an old, modified installation and reported no errors in a manual test of an up-to-date version. This thread does not establish a universal defect in supported releases. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/12267
- [statement] Operational recommendation: reserve pages for actionable incidents and remove duplicate pages. For routine Freqtrade Telegram traffic, silent delivers a message without sound or vibration, while off suppresses that message type. The recommendation combines Google paging criteria with Freqtrade notification controls. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/ · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/blob/develop/docs/telegram-usage.md
- [statement] A snapshot-plus-stream order book requires an explicit bootstrap boundary: queue stream messages, obtain the snapshot, discard messages already covered by its sequence, and replay later messages. Binance and Coinbase Exchange document this pattern. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md
- [statement] For Binance Spot depth, if incoming `U` is greater than the local update ID plus 1, discard the local order book and restart synchronization. Older updates are ignored; quantities replace levels, and zero quantity removes a level. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md
- [statement] Binance warns that a REST depth snapshot covers at most 5000 levels on each side; levels outside the initial snapshot remain unknown until they change. A synchronized local book therefore need not represent every price level. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md
- [statement] Treat candle completion separately from candle receipt: Binance kline payloads include start time, close time and x indicating whether the kline is closed. An arriving update can describe the still-open candle. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://developers.binance.com/docs/binance-spot-api-docs/web-socket-streams
- [statement] Coinbase Exchange heartbeat messages arrive every second for subscribed products and include sequence numbers and last trade IDs for detecting missed messages. These are application-level market-feed checks. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md
- [statement] Delivery guarantees must be checked per channel: Coinbase Exchange warns that matches messages can be dropped and recommends heartbeat plus REST trade backfill, while its level2 channel documentation guarantees delivery of all updates. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md
- [statement] Binance Spot documents planned connection expiry after 24 hours, server ping frames every 20 seconds, disconnection if a pong is not received within a minute, and the requirement to echo the ping payload in the pong. Monitor continuity across these connection lifecycle events. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md
- [statement] Hossein Nejati Javaremi describes batching and aggregation as deliberate feed design choices that reduce message volume while adding latency up to a batch interval; clients must not assume each received message is one exchange event. Coinbase Exchange documents a level2 batch feed using the most recent event time in the batch. (medium confidence) — https://hosseinnejati.medium.com/market-data-distribution-order-book-snapshots-deltas-and-websocket-feed-design-466ba56a0c23 · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md
- [statement] Monitor transport liveness separately from market-data completeness (design inference). Binance documents ping/pong connection checks, while Coinbase supplies heartbeat sequence numbers and last trade IDs to detect missed messages; a healthy connection alone does not establish a complete feed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md
- [statement] Implement order-book integrity checks according to the venue protocol (design inference): Binance prescribes snapshot-plus-buffered-update alignment and gap detection, whereas Kraken documents checksum validation for its book channel. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md · keywords: Crypto autotrading bot monitor reliability and operations · also: https://docs.kraken.com/exchange/guides/websockets/book-checksum-v2
